title: Practice Test 5
description: A full-length adaptive digital SAT practice test written by SAT Ustoz: 98 questions, two modules per section, with an explanation for every question.

questions.passage: Pumice, a volcanic rock filled with tiny gas bubbles, is remarkably ______: some pieces float on the ocean for months, drifting thousands of kilometers before they finally sink.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Rock that floats for months must be very light for its size, so it is **lightweight**. *Dense* is the opposite.

questions.passage: In the earliest years of cinema, most filmmakers kept the camera ______, recording each scene from a single fixed spot as if filming a stage play. Only later did directors begin to move the camera to follow the action.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Filming "from a single fixed spot" means the camera did not move, so it was **stationary**. The next sentence confirms this: only later did cameras move.

questions.passage: Leafcutter ants do not eat the leaves they carry back to their nests. Instead, they use the chopped leaves to ______ a fungus, which they tend in underground chambers and which serves as the colony's main food.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: The ants feed the leaves to a fungus and tend it as food, the way a farmer raises a crop, so they **cultivate** it.

questions.passage: Economist David Morgan cautions that a falling unemployment rate is not always ______ evidence of a strengthening labor market: the rate also falls when discouraged job seekers stop looking for work, since people who are not looking are no longer counted as unemployed.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: A falling rate can mean either more jobs or more people giving up, so it is not **unambiguous** (open to only one reading). *Anecdotal* evidence comes from personal stories, which an unemployment rate is not.

questions.passage: Many dung beetles roll balls of dung away from crowded dung piles, where rivals might steal them, and they travel in remarkably straight lines while doing so. Researchers have long known that the beetles can keep their bearings using the Sun or the Moon. __Some beetles, however, stay on course even on moonless nights, when neither is visible.__ Experiments in a planetarium later showed that these beetles can orient themselves using the faint band of light from the Milky Way.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It presents an observation that the explanation in the previous sentence cannot fully account for.
It offers evidence that dung beetles depend mainly on the Moon to navigate.
It describes a flaw in the planetarium experiments mentioned in the final sentence.
It explains why dung beetles move their dung away from crowded piles.
questions.explanation: The Sun-and-Moon explanation cannot explain straight travel on moonless nights. The underlined sentence raises that puzzle, which the planetarium experiments then solve.

questions.passage: Film histories often describe the arrival of synchronized sound in the late 1920s as a sudden revolution that ended the silent era almost overnight. Historian Margaret Hale points out, however, that many theaters in smaller towns went on showing silent films for years, because installing sound equipment was expensive. In her view, the shift to sound was less a single turning point than a gradual process whose pace depended on local economic conditions.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
choices: To argue that synchronized sound had little lasting influence on the way films were made
To explain why theaters in large cities adopted sound equipment before the technology was reliable
To present a historian's view that a major change in cinema spread more gradually and unevenly than is often assumed
To criticize film historians for overlooking the artistic achievements of silent films
questions.explanation: The text sets up the "sudden revolution" story and then gives Hale's view that the change was gradual and depended on local conditions. She never says sound had *little lasting influence*, only that it spread slowly.

questions.passage:
**Text 1**
Volcanologists have traditionally treated a sharp rise in small earthquakes beneath a volcano as the most dependable sign that an eruption is near. The quakes, the reasoning goes, occur as rising magma forces its way through the surrounding rock.

**Text 2**
Geophysicist Kenji Watanabe and colleagues reviewed monitoring records from dozens of volcanoes. Swarms of small earthquakes came before many eruptions, but they also occurred often with no eruption following. Swarms accompanied by measurable swelling of the ground, however, were far more likely to end in eruptions, so the team recommends tracking both signals together.
questions.prompt: Based on the texts, how would Watanabe and colleagues (Text 2) most likely respond to the traditional view described in Text 1?
choices: By claiming that earthquakes beneath volcanoes are not caused by rising magma
By arguing that earthquake swarms are a less dependable warning on their own than that view assumes, though they become more informative when combined with evidence of ground swelling
By agreeing that earthquake swarms reliably signal an eruption whenever they occur
By recommending that monitoring of ground swelling replace earthquake monitoring entirely
questions.explanation: Text 2 found many swarms with no eruption afterward, so swarms alone are less reliable than Text 1 assumes. The team still uses them, together with ground swelling, which rules out *replace earthquake monitoring entirely*.

questions.passage: The Himalayas stretch for about 2,400 kilometers across South Asia, from Pakistan through India and Nepal to Bhutan. Although they formed long ago, the mountains are still rising. The slow collision between the Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates continues to squeeze the region, pushing the ranges upward and causing frequent earthquakes.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: The Himalayas are the oldest mountains in South Asia.
The Himalayas continue to rise because of an ongoing collision between tectonic plates.
Earthquakes in the Himalayas have become less common over time.
The Indian and Eurasian plates stopped moving long ago.
questions.explanation: The text says the mountains are **still rising** and explains why: the plates are still colliding. The other choices are not stated or contradict the text.

questions.passage:
The following text is from a short story. Nora, a set designer, is visiting the film studio where her father once worked.

The studio's backlot was quieter than Nora remembered. The painted street where her father had built shopfronts out of plywood was still standing, though its colors had faded to the gray of old photographs. She pressed her palm against a door that had never opened onto anything and was surprised to find that it still felt, somehow, like the entrance to somewhere.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Although the old set is faded and was never real, it still gives Nora a sense of possibility.
Nora is upset to discover that her father's street set has been torn down.
Nora realizes that her father built his sets carelessly.
Nora decides to repaint the street set in its original colors.
questions.explanation: The set is faded and the door leads nowhere, yet it still feels like "the entrance to somewhere." The set is still standing, so it was not torn down.

questions.passage: Entomologist Rebecca Stone hypothesizes that males of a certain firefly species flash in unison because females of the species respond more readily to many lights flashing together than to scattered, unsynchronized flashes.
questions.prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Stone's hypothesis?
choices: Males of the species flash more often on warm nights than on cool nights.
In a laboratory, females flashed back more often at groups of small lights blinking in unison than at the same number of lights blinking at random times.
Synchronized flashing has been observed in several firefly species on different continents.
Females of the species fly shorter distances than males do.
questions.explanation: The hypothesis is about how females respond. Only this finding compares female responses to synchronized and random flashing, and females preferred the synchronized lights.

questions.passage: Studying a region where several large warehouses opened within two years, economist Olivia Grant argues that the warehouses raised wages not only for their own employees but also for workers at nearby retail stores, which had to raise pay to keep employees from leaving for warehouse jobs.
questions.prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Grant's argument?
choices: Warehouse employees in the region earned more per hour than retail employees did both before and after the warehouses opened.
Several retail stores in the region closed during the two years in which the warehouses opened.
Most people hired by the new warehouses had been unemployed rather than working in retail.
Retail wages rose faster in towns within commuting distance of the new warehouses than in similar towns farther away, and the gap appeared only after the warehouses began hiring.
questions.explanation: The argument is about a spillover to retail pay. Only this finding ties faster retail wage growth to nearness to the warehouses and to the timing of their hiring. The finding about previously unemployed hires would weaken the argument.

questions.passage: Architecture students measured indoor temperatures at 3:00 p.m. on a hot July day in four buildings in Seville. They note that the building with the thickest walls was the coolest, but that wall thickness alone does not explain their results: ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
choices: the monastery, with walls 90 centimeters thick, was 27°C at 3:00 p.m.
the apartment block had the thinnest walls of the four buildings, at 30 centimeters.
the office without a courtyard was the warmest of the four buildings, at 34°C.
the two offices had walls of the same thickness, yet the office with a courtyard was 6 degrees cooler than the one without.
questions.explanation: To show that thickness alone does not explain the temperatures, you need buildings with equal walls but different temperatures. Both offices have 40 cm walls, yet they differ by 34 − 28 = 6 degrees.

questions.passage: Volcanic ash that falls on farmland can damage crops in the short term, but it also contains minerals, such as potassium and phosphorus, that plants need. Over years and decades, the ash weathers and releases these minerals into the soil. This helps explain why farmers in many volcanic regions ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: continue to cultivate land on the slopes of active volcanoes despite the risk of eruptions.
avoid planting crops in soil that contains volcanic ash.
harvest their largest crops in the year immediately after an eruption.
rarely experience crop damage from eruptions.
questions.explanation: Over time, ash makes the soil fertile, which explains why farmers stay on volcanic slopes. The text says fresh ash damages crops, so the year right after an eruption would not bring the best harvest.

questions.passage: In some species of paper wasp, several queens often start a nest together and settle conflicts through a dominance hierarchy, in which each wasp must keep track of which rivals it has already fought. Biologists have found that one such species has highly variable facial markings, and its members can learn to recognize one another's faces. A closely related species whose queens almost always start nests alone has nearly uniform faces, and its members perform poorly on face-learning tests. These findings suggest that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: facial markings in paper wasps serve mainly to attract mates.
paper wasps that start nests alone are less intelligent in general than those that start nests in groups.
the ability to recognize individuals may have developed in the first species because living among rival queens made that ability useful.
the second species will develop variable facial markings if its queens begin starting nests together.
questions.explanation: Face recognition shows up in the species whose queens must keep track of rivals and not in the species whose queens live alone, which suggests the social setting made it useful. The findings concern face learning only, not *intelligence in general*.

questions.passage: The documentary Snow Line was filmed entirely in the mountains near ______ the crew spent four months living in tents above the tree line.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Both parts are complete sentences, so they need a semicolon. A comma alone, even with *in fact*, creates a comma splice.

questions.passage: Built in the first century, the Pont du Gard near ______ is one of the best-preserved Roman aqueduct bridges in Europe.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: No punctuation belongs between the subject ("the Pont du Gard near Nîmes") and its verb "is."

questions.passage: The desert ______ which can travel up to 150 kilometers in a single day as part of a swarm, is one of the most destructive agricultural pests in the world.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The "which" clause adds extra information and is closed by the comma after "swarm," so it must open with a comma too.

questions.passage: Early sound-film cameras were so noisy that microphones on the set picked up their ______ studios placed each camera, along with its operator, inside a soundproof booth.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Two complete sentences joined by the transition "as a result" need a semicolon before it and a comma after it. The other choices create a comma splice or put the semicolon in the wrong place.

questions.passage: The ants in a single army ant colony ______ able to link their bodies together to form living bridges across gaps on the forest floor.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The subject is the plural "ants," not "colony," so the verb is **are**.

questions.passage: When their studio closed in 1961, the two ______ hand-cranked cameras, which had been used to film nearly every scene of their early comedies, were donated to a museum in Prague.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The cameras belong to two directors ("their early comedies"), so the plural possessive **directors'** is needed.

questions.passage: Among the most unusual features of architect Inès Moreau's design for a new library in Lisbon ______ a roof assembled from thousands of interlocking ceramic tiles.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The sentence is inverted: the subject, "a roof," comes after the verb and is singular, so the verb is **is**. "Features" is not the subject.

questions.passage: Large volcanic eruptions can send sulfur dioxide high into the atmosphere, where it forms tiny droplets that reflect sunlight back into space. ______ a major eruption is sometimes followed by a year or two of slightly cooler temperatures around the world.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Cooler temperatures are a result of the droplets reflecting sunlight, so **Consequently** fits.

questions.passage: Most animated films of the 1930s were made from drawings, with each frame drawn and painted by hand. Stop-motion animators, ______ built small physical models and photographed them, moving each figure slightly between shots.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Stop-motion used models instead of drawings, which contrasts with the method in the first sentence.

questions.passage: When a supermarket chain installed self-checkout machines, analysts predicted that it would sharply cut its workforce. The number of cashier positions at the chain did decline. ______ total employment at its stores held steady, because many workers who had once operated registers moved into jobs restocking shelves, helping customers, and preparing online orders.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The text grants that cashier jobs fell, then says total jobs held steady anyway, so a concession like **Even so** is needed. *Accordingly* would wrongly present steady employment as a result of the decline.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Air moves through networks of tunnels in some termite mounds, helping to regulate conditions inside.
• The Eastgate Centre is an office and shopping complex in Harare, Zimbabwe, that opened in 1996.
• Its ventilation system was modeled on the way air circulates through termite mounds.
• The building uses much less energy for cooling than conventional buildings of similar size.
questions.prompt: The student wants to explain what inspired the design of the Eastgate Centre's ventilation system. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The Eastgate Centre, an office and shopping complex in Harare, Zimbabwe, opened in 1996.
The ventilation system of the Eastgate Centre in Harare, Zimbabwe, was modeled on the way air circulates through termite mounds.
Air moves through networks of tunnels in some termite mounds.
The Eastgate Centre uses much less energy for cooling than conventional buildings of similar size.
questions.explanation: Only this choice names the source of the design idea: the way air moves through termite mounds.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Researchers surveyed 1,500 workers in three cities about how they found their current jobs.
• 46% found their jobs through friends or relatives.
• 31% found their jobs through online job sites.
• 23% found their jobs through other means, such as job fairs or newspaper ads.
questions.prompt: The student wants to emphasize the importance of personal connections in finding a job. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Researchers surveyed 1,500 workers in three cities about how they found their current jobs.
Of the workers surveyed, 31% found their jobs through online job sites.
Nearly half of the workers surveyed (46%) found their current jobs through friends or relatives, more than through any other method.
Some workers found their jobs through job fairs or newspaper ads.
questions.explanation: Friends and relatives are personal connections, and 46% is the largest share. Only this choice makes that point.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Mauna Loa, on the island of Hawaii, is a shield volcano.
• Shield volcanoes erupt runny lava that spreads over wide areas, building broad mountains with gentle slopes.
• Mayon, in the Philippines, is a stratovolcano.
• Stratovolcanoes erupt thicker lava and ash that pile up in layers, building steep, cone-shaped mountains.
questions.prompt: The student wants to contrast the shapes of the two volcanoes and explain the difference. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Mauna Loa and Mayon are both volcanoes, one in Hawaii and the other in the Philippines.
Mauna Loa, a shield volcano, has broad, gentle slopes built by runny lava that spreads widely, whereas Mayon, a stratovolcano, is steep and cone-shaped because thicker lava and ash pile up in layers.
Mayon, a stratovolcano in the Philippines, erupts thicker lava and ash that pile up in layers.
Shield volcanoes such as Mauna Loa erupt runny lava that spreads over wide areas.
questions.explanation: The goal has two parts: contrast the shapes and explain the difference. Only this choice describes both volcanoes' shapes and the kind of eruption that builds each.

questions.passage: The architect chose large south-facing windows so that the classrooms would be ______ with natural light, even on short winter days.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Large windows let in light, so the rooms would be **filled** with it. *Darkened* is the opposite.

questions.passage: Crickets are most ______ at night: during the day they hide under rocks and leaves, but after sunset the males begin chirping loudly to attract mates.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Hiding by day and chirping after sunset means crickets do most of their activity at night, so they are most **active** then.

questions.passage: The director was famously ______ about details: she once reshot an entire scene because a clock in the background showed the wrong time.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Reshooting a scene over a small clock error shows extreme care with details, which is what **meticulous** means. *Careless* is the opposite.

questions.passage: Although the factory's owners expected the new machines to ______ the need for workers, the plant actually hired more employees, because the machines allowed it to accept far more orders.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: "Although" sets up a contrast with hiring more workers, so the owners expected the machines to remove, or **eliminate**, the need for workers.

questions.passage: Geysers form where underground water is heated by hot rock deep below the surface. As the water heats, pressure builds in narrow underground channels until water and steam burst upward through an opening in the ground. The eruption releases the pressure, and the cycle begins again as the channels refill with water.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
choices: To argue that geysers should be protected from tourists
To explain the process that causes geysers to erupt
To describe where the world's largest geysers are found
questions.explanation: The text walks through the steps of an eruption, from heating to pressure to release, so its purpose is to explain how geysers erupt.

questions.passage: Traditional houses in the old quarters of Marrakesh were built around an inner courtyard. __Their thick earthen walls facing the street usually had few or no windows.__ This design kept hot, dusty street air out while letting light and breezes reach the rooms from the shaded courtyard.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It introduces a problem that the houses' builders were unable to solve.
It compares the houses of Marrakesh with those of other cities.
It describes a feature of the houses that the final sentence then explains.
It explains why few houses in Marrakesh had courtyards.
questions.explanation: The underlined sentence describes the windowless street walls, and the last sentence explains why they were built that way ("This design kept hot, dusty street air out").

questions.passage:
**Text 1**
Some film distributors argue that black-and-white classics seem old-fashioned to modern viewers and that these films should be digitally colorized so that more people will watch them.

**Text 2**
Film historian Paul Mercer points out that the makers of black-and-white films planned their lighting, sets, and costumes for a world without color. A costume that looked striking in shades of gray might have been an unappealing color in real life. Adding color afterward, he argues, replaces the look the filmmakers carefully designed with one they never intended.
questions.prompt: Based on the texts, how would Mercer (Text 2) most likely respond to the distributors' proposal in Text 1?
choices: By agreeing that colorized versions would attract larger audiences to classic films
By arguing that colorizing the films would alter visual choices that the original filmmakers made deliberately
By claiming that modern viewers prefer black-and-white films to color films
By suggesting that black-and-white films were cheaper to make than color films
questions.explanation: Mercer says filmmakers designed their films for black and white, so adding color changes what they intended. That is an objection to the distributors' plan.

questions.passage: Caddisfly larvae live on the bottoms of streams, where they face hungry fish and strong currents. To protect themselves, many species build portable cases around their bodies, gluing together grains of sand, tiny pebbles, or bits of plants with a silk they produce. The larvae carry these cases with them as they move and enlarge them as they grow.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Caddisfly larvae are the main food of most stream fish.
Caddisflies spend their entire lives as larvae.
Caddisfly larvae avoid streams with strong currents.
Many caddisfly larvae protect themselves by building cases from materials found in their surroundings.
questions.explanation: Every sentence after the first describes the protective cases the larvae build from sand, pebbles, or plants.

questions.passage:
The following text is from a short story. Hannah, a young engineer, is starting her first job at a construction site.

On her first morning, Hannah arrived with a new hard hat and a folder of drawings she had checked three times. The foreman glanced at the folder, then handed it back without opening it. "Drawings are what we hope will happen," he said, nodding toward the half-finished walls. "Spend today watching what actually does."
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: A foreman suggests that Hannah will learn more by watching the work on the site than by studying her plans.
Hannah is criticized for the errors in her drawings.
The foreman refuses to let Hannah work at the site.
Hannah decides that her engineering training was a waste of time.
questions.explanation: The foreman contrasts plans ("what we hope will happen") with real work ("what actually does") and tells her to watch. He never opens the folder, so he points out no errors.

questions.passage: A human resources researcher hypothesizes that employees who are allowed to choose their own working hours take fewer sick days than employees with fixed schedules.
questions.prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the researcher's hypothesis?
choices: Employees with flexible hours said that they enjoyed their jobs.
Most employees at the company preferred to start work early in the morning.
Employees with fixed schedules worked in larger offices than employees with flexible hours.
At one company, employees with flexible hours took an average of 4 sick days per year, compared with 7 for employees with fixed schedules.
questions.explanation: Only this choice compares sick days for the two kinds of schedules, and the flexible group took fewer.

questions.passage: Geologist Maria Santos claims that a layer of volcanic ash found in the mud at the bottom of several lakes across a region came from a single large eruption rather than from several smaller ones.
questions.prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Santos's claim?
choices: The ash layer is thicker in some lakes than in others.
Several volcanoes in the region have erupted within the past 10,000 years.
The lakes in the region formed at different times.
The ash in every lake has the same distinctive chemical makeup, and in each lake the layer dates to the same year.
questions.explanation: Identical chemistry and identical dates point to one eruption. Several active volcanoes in the region would, if anything, suggest more than one source.

questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
questions.explanation: 48 is the largest number in the table, and it belongs to the 1970s.

questions.passage: Mud brick, made from clay and straw dried in the sun, absorbs heat slowly during the day and releases it slowly at night. In desert regions where days are hot and nights are cold, buildings made of mud brick therefore tend to ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: heat up quickly in the afternoon.
stay cooler during the day and warmer at night than the air outside.
need more fuel for heating at night than other buildings.
be found only near large rivers.
questions.explanation: Slow absorption keeps rooms cool by day, and slow release keeps them warm at night.

questions.passage: Some species of ants tend aphids, small insects that feed on plant sap and release a sugary liquid called honeydew. The ants eat the honeydew and, in return, protect the aphids from ladybugs and other predators. Researchers who remove the ants from some plants would therefore most likely find that ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: aphids on those plants produce more honeydew than before.
aphids on those plants are eaten by predators more often than aphids on plants where the ants remain.
those plants become home to larger numbers of aphids than before.
questions.explanation: The ants protect aphids from predators, so without the ants, more aphids would be eaten. That also means there would be fewer aphids, not more.

questions.passage: Before the invention of powerful electric ______ filmmakers often shot their scenes outdoors in bright sunlight.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: A comma separates the introductory phrase "Before...lights" from the main sentence. A semicolon or colon would need a complete sentence before it.

questions.passage: The architect relied on two local ______ fired brick from nearby kilns and oak from the Loire Valley.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: A colon introduces the two materials after a complete sentence. A semicolon would need a complete sentence after it.

questions.passage: Victor Lanz's first feature ______ a black-and-white drama set in a mill town, won a prize at a regional film festival in 1968.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "A black-and-white drama set in a mill town" renames the film and closes with a comma, so it must open with a comma too.

questions.passage: The thick walls and small, shaded windows of traditional desert ______ help keep indoor rooms cool during the hottest hours of the day.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The subject ("The thick walls...homes") runs straight into its verb "help," so no punctuation belongs between them.

questions.passage: Last summer, a team of geologists ______ samples of hardened lava from the slopes of the volcano.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Last summer" places the action in the past, so the past tense **collected** is needed.

questions.passage: Architects in hot climates often design roofs that extend well beyond a building's walls, because ______ shade the windows below from the midday sun.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The pronoun refers to the plural "roofs" and goes with the plural verb "shade," so it must be **they**.

questions.passage: Although the volcano has been quiet for decades, scientists still monitor ______ slopes for signs of swelling.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The slopes belong to the singular "volcano," so the possessive is **its**. *It's* means "it is," and *its'* is not a word.

questions.passage: Desert locusts usually live alone and avoid one another. ______ when heavy rains bring many of them together, they change color and behavior and begin to form huge swarms.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Forming swarms is the opposite of living alone, so a contrast word is needed.

questions.passage: Apprenticeship programs let workers earn wages while they learn a trade. ______ the programs give employers a chance to train workers in the specific skills their businesses need.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The second sentence adds another benefit of apprenticeships, so **In addition** fits.

questions.passage: Engineers in earthquake-prone regions design buildings to sway slightly during an earthquake rather than resist the shaking rigidly, since rigid structures are more likely to crack. ______ many tall buildings in these regions rest on flexible bearings that absorb some of the ground's motion.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Flexible bearings follow from the goal of letting buildings sway, so the second sentence is a result of the first.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Obsidian is a type of volcanic glass.
• It forms when lava cools so quickly that crystals do not have time to grow.
• Its broken edges can be extremely sharp.
• Ancient peoples used obsidian to make knives and arrowheads.
questions.prompt: The student wants to explain how obsidian forms. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Ancient peoples used obsidian to make knives and arrowheads.
The broken edges of obsidian can be extremely sharp.
Obsidian is a type of volcanic glass.
Obsidian is a volcanic glass that forms when lava cools so quickly that crystals do not have time to grow.
questions.explanation: Only this choice tells how obsidian forms: lava cools too quickly for crystals to grow.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The Giralda in Seville, Spain, was completed as a minaret in 1198 and later became the bell tower of Seville Cathedral.
• It is built mainly of brick arranged in decorative patterns.
• The bell tower of Pisa Cathedral in Italy, known as the Leaning Tower of Pisa, was completed in 1372.
• It is built mainly of white marble.
questions.prompt: The student wants to emphasize the difference in age between the two towers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Completed in 1198, the Giralda in Seville is more than 170 years older than the Leaning Tower of Pisa, which was completed in 1372.
The Giralda is built mainly of brick, while the Leaning Tower of Pisa is built mainly of white marble.
The Leaning Tower of Pisa is the bell tower of Pisa Cathedral in Italy.
The Giralda in Seville, Spain, is built mainly of brick arranged in decorative patterns.
questions.explanation: The goal is a difference in age, which needs both completion dates: 1372 − 1198 = 174 years. The brick-and-marble choice compares materials instead.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Economists studied 2,000 delivery drivers who used an app that let them choose when to start and stop working.
• The economists compared the hours each driver worked on a given day with the driver's hourly earnings that day.
• On days when hourly earnings were high, many drivers stopped working earlier than usual.
• The economists concluded that many drivers aim for a daily earnings target rather than a fixed number of hours.
questions.prompt: The student wants to describe the method the economists used in their study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: On days when their hourly earnings were high, many app-based delivery drivers stopped working earlier than usual.
The economists compared the daily working hours of 2,000 app-based delivery drivers with how much the drivers earned per hour on each day.
The economists concluded that many drivers aim for a daily earnings target rather than a fixed number of hours.
Delivery drivers who use apps can choose when to start and stop working.
questions.explanation: A method is what the researchers did. Only this choice describes what the economists compared; the others give a result, the conclusion, or background.

questions.passage: Because the rock layers at the base of the canyon were laid down over millions of years without interruption, geologist Owen Fletcher regards them as an unusually ______ archive: whereas most rock sequences are riddled with gaps where layers eroded away, these layers preserve a nearly complete history of the region's climate.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: The colon contrasts these layers with sequences "riddled with gaps": nothing is missing from them, so they are **intact**. *Fragmentary* describes the gap-filled sequences instead.

questions.passage: Although the director's films were often praised as loose and improvised, her assistant's notebooks reveal that their seemingly spontaneous moments were in fact ______: scenes that appear to unfold by accident were rehearsed dozens of times.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Scenes rehearsed dozens of times were carefully arranged in advance, or **orchestrated**. *Unscripted* is what the moments only seemed to be.

questions.passage: In her study of hiring in the textile industry, economist Julia Brandt finds that employers' stated preference for experienced workers is largely ______: when her team sent employers pairs of otherwise identical applications that differed only in years of experience, the two applications received callbacks at nearly the same rate.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Employers say they prefer experience but treat the applications the same, so the preference exists mostly in name: it is **nominal**. *Pervasive* (widespread) ignores the evidence that the preference has little effect.

questions.passage: Individually, army ants have strikingly ______ navigational abilities: the ants are nearly blind and simply follow chemical trails left by others, so a group that loses its trail may march in a circle for hours. Yet colonies of these ants carry out coordinated raids across large areas of forest floor.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Being nearly blind and marching in circles shows very basic, or **rudimentary**, abilities. *Sophisticated* fits the colony, not the individual ant, as "Yet" makes clear.

questions.passage: Visitors to the apartment blocks built in Tbilisi in the 1970s and 1980s often notice the large mosaic panels on their outer walls, which depict grape harvests, space flights, and scenes from local legends. Architectural historian Daniel Weiss argues that these panels should not be dismissed as decoration added to otherwise ordinary buildings. Because the panels were often planned together with the buildings themselves, he contends, they gave architects one of the few ways to express regional character in structures whose layouts followed standard designs approved in Moscow.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
choices: To argue that standard building designs prevented architects in Tbilisi from expressing any regional character
To describe the subjects most often shown in the mosaic panels on Tbilisi's buildings
To present a historian's argument that a feature of certain buildings was more significant than it might appear
To explain why building designs approved in Moscow were poorly suited to Tbilisi's climate
questions.explanation: The text reports Weiss's claim that the panels were more than decoration. The first wrong choice goes too far: in his view, the panels *were* a way to express regional character.

questions.passage: Many species of firefly produce patterns of flashes to attract mates. Females of some species, however, imitate the flash patterns of other species. __When a male of another species approaches, expecting to find a mate, the female captures and eats him.__ Biologists have found that the imitators gain more than a meal: by eating these males, they acquire defensive chemicals, which they cannot produce themselves, that make them distasteful to spiders and birds.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It describes the outcome of the behavior introduced in the previous sentence, an outcome that the final sentence shows has an additional benefit.
It offers an example of the courtship behavior described in the first sentence.
It presents a hypothesis that the final sentence calls into question.
It explains how males of the imitated species avoid being captured.
questions.explanation: The previous sentence introduces the imitation, and the underlined sentence tells what it leads to: the male is eaten. The final sentence adds a further benefit. The female is hunting, not courting, so the sentence is not an example of mating behavior.

questions.passage:
**Text 1**
For decades, many economists held that raising the minimum wage must reduce employment among low-wage workers. If labor becomes more expensive, the reasoning went, employers will simply hire fewer people.

**Text 2**
Economist Michael Foster notes that this reasoning assumes employers cannot set wages below what workers would earn in a competitive market. In towns dominated by a single large employer, he argues, workers have few alternatives, so the employer can hold wages down. In such places, a moderate rise in the minimum wage could draw more people into the workforce without reducing the number of jobs.
questions.prompt: Based on the texts, how would Foster (Text 2) most likely respond to the reasoning presented in Text 1?
choices: He would agree that higher minimum wages reduce employment but argue that the benefits to workers outweigh this cost.
He would claim that it applies only to towns dominated by a single large employer.
He would argue that it rests on an assumption that does not hold in labor markets where workers have few alternative employers.
He would contend that raising the minimum wage increases employment regardless of local conditions.
questions.explanation: Foster identifies a hidden assumption in Text 1 and says it fails where one employer dominates. He does not grant that jobs are lost, and his claim is limited to particular towns, not "regardless of local conditions."

questions.passage: Film restorers working on damaged silent films face a dilemma. Many such films survive only in copies made decades after their release, and these copies often differ from the versions that audiences first saw: scenes were cut by censors, title cards were rewritten for new markets, and colors added by hand-tinting were lost when the films were copied onto black-and-white stock. Restorer Isabelle Laurent argues that every restoration is therefore an interpretation, and she insists that restorers document each choice they make so that viewers can see where a restored film departs from the surviving evidence.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Hand-tinted color was the feature of silent films most often lost in later copies.
Restorers should stop trying to recreate silent films as audiences first saw them.
Because surviving copies of silent films may differ from the originals in many ways, a restorer argues that restorers should be open about the decisions they make.
Censorship was the main reason that silent films were altered after their release.
questions.explanation: The text explains why surviving copies are unreliable and ends with Laurent's call to document every choice. She wants restorers to be transparent, not to stop restoring, and the text never ranks the causes of change.

questions.passage:
The following text is from a poem. The speaker describes a scene at dawn.

The cranes along the river stand unmoving,
their long necks bent above the unfinished towers,
as if they, too, were waiting for the morning
to tell them what the city means to build.
Below, the workers gather with their thermoses,
and steel begins to answer to their voices.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: The speaker portrays a construction site as still and expectant until the arriving workers set it in motion.
The speaker describes birds gathering along a river before they fly away for the day.
The speaker mourns the loss of old buildings that were torn down to make room for new towers.
The speaker suggests that the workers are reluctant to begin a dangerous job.
questions.explanation: The "cranes" stand above "unfinished towers," and steel responds to the workers, so they are construction cranes described as if they were birds. The scene waits until the workers arrive and work begins.

questions.passage: Volcanologist Teresa Alvarez hypothesizes that eruptions of a particular volcano in a region with distinct wet and dry seasons are often triggered when heavy seasonal rains soak deep into the ground, raising the pressure in the rock around the volcano's magma chamber.
questions.prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Alvarez's hypothesis?
choices: The volcano receives more rainfall each year than any other volcano in the region.
Over the past century, the volcano's eruptions have begun far more often in the two months after the end of the wet season than at any other time of year.
When rainwater meets hot rock during an eruption, the resulting steam makes the volcano's explosions more violent.
The volcano's magma chamber lies closer to the surface than those of most other volcanoes in the region.
questions.explanation: If soaking rains trigger eruptions, eruptions should cluster soon after the wet season, which is what this finding shows. The steam choice is about how violent an eruption is once it has begun, not what starts it.

questions.passage: Economists studying a city's labor market recorded wage growth and the share of workers who changed employers in four industries over one year. They note that faster wage growth in an industry did not necessarily mean that more of its workers changed jobs: ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
choices: construction had the fastest wage growth of the four industries, 6.2%, and 18% of its workers changed employers.
health care had the smallest share of workers who changed employers, 9%.
manufacturing had faster wage growth than health care, 5.4% versus 4.1%, and a larger share of its workers changed employers, 11% versus 9%.
construction had faster wage growth than retail, 6.2% versus 3.0%, yet a smaller share of construction workers changed employers, 18% versus 24%.
questions.explanation: The claim needs an industry with faster wage growth but fewer job changers than another industry. Construction versus retail shows exactly that. The manufacturing choice shows the opposite pattern.

He concluded that a trail became more attractive as more ants marked it, but only up to a point: ______

a trail marked by 200 ants drew 90 followers, barely more than the 87 drawn by a trail marked by 50 ants.
the unmarked trail drew the fewest followers, 12.
a trail marked by 50 ants drew 87 followers, more than twice as many as a trail marked by 10 ants.
